stories.summary: Fantasy football rankings from Matt Bowen, Mike Clay, Tristan H. Cockcroft, Daniel Dopp, Eric Karabell, Liz Loza, Eric Moody and Field Yates.

stories.headline: The top reason to watch every NHL team in the Frozen Frenzy
stories.summary: From elite scorers to exciting rookies to legit drama, here's what we love about all 32.
stories.body:
Hockey's greatest buffet returns on Tuesday, Oct. 13, as the Frozen Frenzy returns to ESPN. All 32 teams battle on the same night, giving fans a chance to sample the contenders, pretenders and those teams that are downright fascinating so far this season.

A few notes from last October's Frenzy:

109 goals were scored in 16 games
Road teams were 9-6-1
Five games went into overtime or a shootout

ESPN has a tripleheader featuring the New Jersey Devils at the Detroit Red Wings (6 p.m. ET); the Colorado Avalanche at the Dallas Stars (8:30 p.m. ET); and the Boston Bruins facing the San Jose Sharks in the nightcap (11 p.m. ET). The start times for all 16 games are staggered to maximize channel surfing on NHL Power Play on the ESPN App.

In addition, there are five hours of continuous Frozen Frenzy whip-around coverage hosted by John Buccigross and Kevin Weekes on ESPN2, Disney+ and the ESPN App.

That's a lot of hockey. Luckily, there are a lot of reasons to watch it.

Here are compelling players, trends and storylines for all 32 teams to keep in mind as the Frozen Frenzy washes over you:

Atlantic Division

Boston Bruins
Captain Pasta

David Pastrnak was named the 28th captain in this Original Six franchise's history, and for good reason: Very few star players in the NHL mean as much to their team's fortunes as Pasta does for the B's.

Since 2022-23, Pastrnak has strung together four straight 100-point seasons. He has 436 points in 329 games during that span, including 254 goals. The next-highest scorer for Boston trails him by 206 points since 2022 (Pavel Zacha, 230). It's Pasta's world.

Buffalo Sabres
Playoff rematch

The Sabres weren't simply satisfied with ending their NHL-record 14-season playoff drought. Buffalo had its eyes on a larger prize after eliminating the Bruins in six games in the opening round.

But the Montreal Canadiens shattered those dreams, eliminating the Sabres on a Game 7 overtime goal by Alex Newhook. It was a series with some animosity. One assumes that ill will carries over to the first regular-season meeting between the teams since that playoff battle.

Detroit Red Wings
The Dylan Larkin drama

The most compelling ongoing hockey soap opera is playing out in Detroit. Captain Dylan Larkin requested a trade despite having five seasons left on an eight-year contract with the Red Wings. Possessing a no-trade clause, Larkin provided just three teams to whom he would accept a trade -- and none of the three had the personnel or cap space to make a deal for him.

Larkin's list has reportedly expanded, but that gambit was enough to catch the eye (and a little ire) of commissioner Gary Bettman, who said the league will keep an eye on how players are using their trade protection to force moves to specific destinations.

Meanwhile, Larkin rejoined the Red Wings, who stripped him of his captaincy. He was booed on opening night, while standing in street clothes, injured. When he returned to the lineup, he was booed again. In a surreal moment, the Red Wings center was cheered by fans in Montreal who chanted "We want Larkin!" in an effort to convince him to waive his trade protection for a Canadian destination. What twist comes next?

Florida Panthers
The Tkachuks

While initially refusing to succumb to the urge, Panthers coach Paul Maurice finally gave fans what they've been asking to see: truculent brothers Matthew and Brady Tkachuk centered by the equally coarse Sam Bennett.

Before the season, Maurice said putting these three provocateurs together would result in them being "in jail before the puck drops." But now he admits the trio "brought a little juice" to a team missing both Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand to injury.

Montreal Canadiens
Can Juraj Slafkovsky snap the slump?

Slafkovsky, the first overall pick in the 2022 draft, leveled up to star status last season with 30 goals and 43 assists (73 points), setting new career highs. But he has just one goal in five games this season, as part of a quiet offensive start for the Habs overall.

Slafkovsky was moved off Montreal's top line in favor of free agent signee Chris Kreider, and then saw new linemate Ivan Demidov get injured. Slafkovsky was shifted back to the top line with Nick Suzuki and Cole Caufield recently, but they've yet to recapture the magic.

Ottawa Senators
Brady who?

The Senators traded captain Brady Tkachuk to the Florida Panthers -- a.k.a. "his brother's team" -- after Tkachuk informed the team he wasn't going to sign a new contract with Ottawa when his deal is up in 2028. Ottawa lost a pace-setting point-per-game player, but based on the early returns they aren't exactly missing him.

The Senators sprinted out to four wins in their first five games thanks to their stout defensive game and a blazing start by Tim Stutzle (eight points), Tkachuk's former linemate. Spite is a heck of a motivator.

Tampa Bay Lightning
High-IQ Nikita Kucherov

The Lightning star made waves before the season when he was asked about how the game has changed in his 13-season NHL career. "The game is faster but very dumb. Low IQ," he told reporters.

Of course, watching the brilliant Kucherov -- who won his second Hart Trophy as NHL MVP last season -- one realizes he's playing high-speed chess while his opponents play tiddlywinks. On Frenzy night, Kucherov leads the Lightning against the Rangers, who defeated the Bolts 5-1 in their season opener.

Toronto Maple Leafs
Gavin McKenna, phenom

It's still mind-blowing to think that the Maple Leafs, one season after star Mitch Marner defected to the Golden Knights, won the draft lottery and the chance to draft another Canadian-born phenom winger -- who doubles as a beacon of hope for the franchise.

McKenna already got a taste of the Toronto media after failing to score in his first three games. He had four points in his next three games. Just 18 years old, McKenna is a young star worth searching out in the Frenzy.

Metropolitan Division

Carolina Hurricanes
Another Washington test

The reigning Stanley Cup champions didn't skip a beat, earning 11 out of 14 points to start the season. Sebastian Aho has been dominant (six goals, five assists) for a team that's getting scoring throughout the lineup -- heck, Mark Jankowski has a four-game goal streak.

But the Canes' lone regulation loss came at the hands of the Capitals, who beat them 5-2 in Raleigh. They get Washington again in the Frozen Frenzy, ready to respond against the team many feel is the Canes' toughest competition in the Metro.

Columbus Blue Jackets
Spotlight on Matthew Knies

The Blue Jackets made the season's biggest trade so far when they sent winger Kirill Marchenko to the Maple Leafs.

Marchenko wanted out, but Columbus was only going to move him for the right trade centerpiece. They jumped at the chance to land Knies, the 23-year-old power winger who scored 52 goals over the past two seasons skating with star Auston Matthews.

In Columbus, Knies will get his own chance to be a "face of the franchise" guy. Perhaps what made him most compelling for the Jackets: He's signed through 2030-31.

New Jersey Devils
The dynamic duo

Jack Hughes is the focal point of the Devils and for good reason: The 25-year-old Olympic hockey legend is one of the NHL's most dynamic talents. But Hughes is never more exciting than when he's buzzing around the ice with New Jersey's other all-world offensive talent: winger Jesper Bratt, 28, who eclipsed a point-per-game pace in two of the past three seasons.

Two players with elite skating ability, pinpoint puckhandling and endless creativity. We're not saying that we want the Devils' game in Detroit to go to the 3-on-3 to see Hughes and Bratt work their magic. But we wouldn't complain if it happened.

New York Islanders
Matthew Schaefer's enthusiasm

Last season's unanimous choice for NHL rookie of the year, Schaefer's personality on and off the ice shifted the vibes for the Islanders. He also established himself as one of the rising stars among defensemen with 59 points in 82 games.

Now 19 years old, Schaefer is skating over 25 minutes per game and pulling off video-game-level moves with his skating. While team executives felt it was a bit early for Schaefer to be ranked No 16 overall in our ESPN NHL player rankings, that's just symbolic of his meteoric rise.

New York Rangers
Life without Igor

The most crushing moment so far in the NHL: Rangers star goalie Igor Shesterkin suffering a season-ending knee injury after five games. Not just because he's one of the best goalies on Earth, but because the Rangers were off to a torrid start in the Metro Division.

They've turned to 24-year-old Dylan Garand to (literally) save their season. He's a great story: someone who put in the time with AHL Hartford over the past few seasons and passed through waivers unclaimed before ascending to the Rangers' crease.

It's his net until veteran Joonas Korpisalo returns from injury -- and potentially beyond that.

Philadelphia Flyers
Averting disaster

In the span of five months, coach Rick Tocchet has seen the Flyers go from winning a playoff round to failing to win a game in this first seven tries this season.

He has heard cheers from fans after snapping a six-season playoff drought to hearing the fans chanting "Fire Tocchet!" at home games. Such is life in Philadelphia sports.

The bottom line: This talented young team has to start turning their fortunes around fast, as they welcome the Seattle Kraken to the City of Brotherly Love.

Pittsburgh Penguins
Crosby's breakout?

Thanks to his legendary preparation, Sidney Crosby is known to start fast, with a career average of 1.20 points per game in the first month of the season.

Through six games last season, the Penguins star captain had three goals and four assists; through six games this season, he's yet to get off the blocks: two assists and a minus-4 rating.

It's just a matter of time before the 39-year-old finds his groove. Does it happen in Chicago during the Frenzy?

Washington Capitals
Ovi's last ride

Alex Ovechkin finally gave a definitive answer to "is this Alex Ovechkin's last NHL season?" when he informed his teammates that this is his last run with the Capitals. (One assumes he'll play at least another season with Dynamo Moscow in the KHL, a scenario Ovechkin hasn't dispelled.)

The NHL's all-time leading goal scorer faces the Hurricanes in the Frenzy, having just scored his first goal of the season -- joining the 930 club in the city that gave us The 9:30 Club.

Central Division

Chicago Blackhawks
Patrick Kane comes home

The cynical reading of Patrick Kane's return to Chicago, where he won three Stanley Cups, was as a nostalgia play designed to distract from the team's current plight. But it will be a kick to see Kane back in a Blackhawks uniform, helping to shape the team's young stars on and off the ice. It's like seeing John Cena return from a prolonged absence to put on the jorts and put over the current young champion.

Hopefully Kane has as much left in the tank as Cena did in his farewell, as the Chicago winger has just one goal and one assist through six games.

Colorado Avalanche
An early test

The Avalanche were the NHL's best team last regular season and pushed all the way to the Western Conference finals before falling apart physically and losing to the Golden Knights.

So far, Colorado has looked dominant at times and vulnerable at other times. Matching up with their longtime division rivals from Dallas will be a good test for both teams but in particular Colorado, to see if Nathan MacKinnon and friends can roll against a talented contender.

Dallas Stars
Jason Robertson makes his case

It was a weird few months for Jason Robertson. The 27-year-old winger finished the second-best goal-scoring season of his career (45 goals) to enter restricted free agency. But there was no long-term contract on which he and the Stars could agree, leading to his rights nearly being traded to Seattle -- a deal denied by Robertson, who didn't want to sign there.

He's an unrestricted free agent next summer and looking to fill the net for a huge payday, in Dallas or elsewhere.

Minnesota Wild
The Quinn Hughes mystery

The Wild made a blockbuster trade for Norris Trophy-winning defenseman Quinn Hughes last season, and he helped turn Minnesota into something of a juggernaut with 48 points in 48 games, skating over 27 minutes per game.

There was confidence that the team would be able to sign Hughes to an extension ahead of free agency next summer ... but that hasn't happened yet, leading to speculation that the defenseman might have something else in his mind regarding his future (i.e. playing with his brothers).

Hughes has started strong for the contending Wild (seven points in five games), who are in Winnipeg for a big divisional game during the Frenzy.

Nashville Predators
Stammer's still got it

At any point in the past 19 years, Steven Stamkos scoring 42 goals wouldn't have been anything out of the ordinary: Only Alex Ovechkin and Sidney Crosby have scored more goals among active players. But the fact that Stamkos did it with the Predators after his first season in Nashville was such a dud probably deserved more attention.

Stamkos has three goals in his first five games this season, again looking very much like ... well, like Steven Stamkos.

St. Louis Blues
Jimmy Snuggerud's second act

After struggling to find his stride, Snuggerud became one of the NHL's top rookie forwards last season after thriving on a line with Dylan Holloway and Robert Thomas.

While that trio has yet to get rolling in 2026-27 -- and watch out for the Blues when it does -- Snuggerud is off to a solid start with three goals in his first five games. He's a big part of what they're building in St. Louis.

Utah Mammoth
Checking the oil

The Mammoth have all the pieces to potentially level up to championship contender status this season. They have strong veteran scorers in Nick Schmaltz and Clayton Keller, and young dynamos such as Dylan Guenther and Logan Cooley. They brought in some leadership in Anders Lee from the Islanders and Vincent Trocheck from the Rangers. Karel Vejmelka is one of the league's most underrated goalies, in back of a defense that features players such as MacKenzie Weegar and Mikhail Sergachev.

How good can they be? Seeing Utah against the surging Oilers will be a great test and one of the Frenzy's best matchups.

Winnipeg Jets
No Helly, no problem

Star goalie Connor Hellebuyck is currently suspended by the Jets after failing to report to camp following his trade demand. Not having the best goalie in the world on the roster is not ideal, but the Jets were determined to thrive without him.

The combination of veteran Stuart Skinner (.920 save percentage) and Capitals depth chart casualty Clay Stevenson (.872) have given the Jets enough goaltending to find themselves in a playoff spot through five games. Eventually, not having Hellebuyck to paper over the deficiencies in their lineup will catch up with them. But not yet, at least.

Pacific Division

Anaheim Ducks
18 million expectations

Leo Carlsson shocked the hockey world by signing an offer sheet from the Flyers that carried an $18 million average annual value, which the Ducks matched. That gave the 21-year-old center the largest cap hit in the NHL this season.

Big paydays change perceptions and expectations. Carlsson hit a career high with 67 points in 70 games last season. He has started strong with eight points in his first five games this season, carrying the extra weight of an $18 million cap hit on his back.

Calgary Flames
Silver linings

It's not expected to be a good year for the rebuilding Flames. Losing their first five games and posting a minus-19 goal differential hasn't dispelled that notion.

So in what could be a rough campaign, attention turns to the future. Can winger Matt Coronato take another step? Can forward Matvei Gridin have a breakout second season? Did defenseman Simon Nemec just need a change in scenery out of New Jersey?

Interesting questions now, but important ones for the future.

Edmonton Oilers
Is this the year?

Edmonton looks like a team possessed to start the season, with Connor McDavid doing Connor McDavid things, Evan Bouchard trying to score his way to a Norris Trophy and Buffalo castoff Devon Levi looking like he maybe ... possibly ... could be their solution in goal.

How much of this is controversial new coach Mike Babcock's doing? Or is it simply McDavid, Leon Draisaitl & Co. coming back with a vengeance after a playoff disappointment, knowing that their window to win a Stanley Cup is shrinking. Whatever the case, the Oilers are playing like a Western Conference favorite.

Los Angeles Kings
The Bread Man

The Kings acquired winger Artemi Panarin from the Rangers last season to bring some offensive flash to a team that sorely lacked it. And that's what he has done: 27 points in 26 games last season, and three goals in his first four games this season.

The 34-year-old winger is playing on the Kings' top line with center Quinton Byfield.

San Jose Sharks
Macklin Celebrini, the next megastar

Celebrini isn't just the future of the NHL. He's also the present. The 20-year-old center was fourth in MVP voting last season with 115 points in 82 games, turning the Sharks into an unexpected playoff contender.

Surrounded by arguably the best assemblage of young talent in the NHL, Celebrini is the league's most exciting player and potentially its first crossover star in decades, with features in The Hollywood Reporter and GQ Magazine already this season.

Seattle Kraken
An early surprise

The Kraken were predicted by many to be in the mushy middle of the standings at best, or closer to the bottom of the conference at worst. But the sixth-year franchise has won four of its first six games with the league's third-best offense, leading to a plus-9 goal differential.

Granted, hanging six goals on the Calgary Flames twice will boast those numbers, but they also hit six against Vegas and Washington. How real are they?

Vancouver Canucks
The Pette-issance

Elias Pettersson scored 39 goals and 103 points in 2022-23, but that might as well have been 20 years ago based on how the Canucks center has played in the past few campaigns. Whether it was injuries or off-ice drama with teammates, there were many theories about why Petey lost his mojo ... as well as the annual hope from Vancouver fans that he could find it again, if only to convince another team to trade for his $11.6 million cap hit (through 2030-31!).

With a new coach in Manny Malhotra, Pettersson has eight points in his first seven games, a promising start for the Pette-issance.

Vegas Golden Knights
Eichel goes for 100

Jack Eichel has been dominant offensively over the past couple of seasons, with 94 points in 77 games and then 90 points in 74 games, the two highest-scoring seasons in Golden Knights history. The star center has sprinted out to a ridiculous two points-per-game average, with 12 points in six games.

Vegas has never had a 100-point season. Eichel seems like he's on a mission to change that, while getting the Golden Knights back to the Stanley Cup Final for a second straight campaign.

stories.headline: Unai Emery keen for Aston Villa to use home advantage in Fenerbahce clash
stories.summary: Aston Villa boss Unai Emery wants his side to enjoy their home comforts once again when they host Fenerbahce in the Champions League.
stories.body:
Aston Villa boss Unai Emery wants his side to enjoy their home comforts once again when they host Fenerbahce in the Champions League.

The side's form at Villa Park has been one of the driving forces behind Villa's rise to the top of the English game, where they are once again competing in the European Cup for the second time in three years.

But they are enduring a tough time of it on home soil this season, having lost two and drawn the other of their opening three games.

That may be in part due to the fact they are only playing in front of three sides this season as the North Stand gets refurbished in time for Euro 2028, with the building site affecting the atmosphere.

But Emery thinks it is time to put it right against the Turkish outfit on Wednesday night.

- Unai Emery 'sad' after Aston Villa draw with Brentford

- How Aston Villa boss Unai Emery rescued Real Unión, his 'family' club, from ruin

"We are realistic about how we are working and improving things," he said at a news conference on Tuesday. "But it is not enough yet, so we are having lots of conversations with the team, in meetings and with videos, practicing too to show improvements in matches.

"At Villa Park, we have not won yet, so it is very important how we can improve things to be closer to winning. Tomorrow is a very good opportunity to do one step forward in those improvements and the players as well to get confidence and feel comfortable.

"Villa Park is for us something very, very special. It should be like the four years that we are here -- how we achieved this as a special place, our fortress. Tomorrow is a new challenge to show it."

Villa's inconsistent start to the season has not been helped by injuries and they have suffered another blow in the build-up to the second round of Champions League fixtures.

Matteo Ruggeri came off at half-time of Saturday's 2-2 draw with Brentford, leaving a gap at left-back with Ian Maatsen still out.

George Hemmings will miss out but Leon Goretzka could be set for a debut as he builds his fitness up following a knee injury which has curtailed the first few weeks of his Villa Park stay.

Brian Madjo and Taylor Harwood-Bellis are ineligible having been left out of the Champions League squad.

"There are negative ways for some players, because they are injured like Ruggeri," Emery said.

"We must try to find solutions as Maatsen is not available. I think he should be in a few days, one week or two weeks joining us.

"Ruggeri, we don't know exactly how long it's going to be, but it will be some weeks that he's going to be out, more than one month. We need to find solutions because [Ian] Maatsen is not yet available.

"I think, the way he is, getting better, he should be joining us in a few days or a week, so it's positive.

"Leon Goretzka is in the squad for tomorrow; George Hemmings is still being with a small pain -- not [available] for tomorrow but maybe on Saturday he can come back

stories.headline: Every team's odds to win the 2026 World Series: Favored Brewers take 2-0 NLCS lead
stories.summary: Every MLB team's odds to win the 2026 World Series as the playoffs continue.
stories.body:
The idea that the Los Angeles Dodgers might not win the World Series in 2026 is starting to become a reality, according to the odds. After losing title favorite status for the first time all season due to a Game 1 loss, the Dodgers also dropped Game 2 of the National League Championship Series and are out to +350 for the championship, their longest odds of the year.

The Milwaukee Brewers, meanwhile, extended their odds lead to +105 after coming into the NLCS with +300 World Series odds. Milwaukee was not expected to be a title contender coming into the season (according to bookmakers) as they started at a 14th-best 35-1.

Either Milwaukee or Los Angeles would likely be favored in the World Series against whichever team comes out of the American League. As of now, that would be the Cleveland Guardians, who stole a road Game 1 of the ALCS from the Tampa Bay Rays and improved their championship odds from +650 to +400. Tampa Bay fell from +330 to +475 with the loss.

Odds by DraftKings at time of publication.

stories.headline: Clarence Seedorf: I understand why Kobbie Mainoo is compared to me
stories.summary: AC Milan and Ajax legend Clarence Seedorf told Manchester United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo that he sees similarities between himself and the England international.
stories.body:
AC Milan and Ajax legend Clarence Seedorf told Manchester United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo that he sees similarities between himself and the England international.

Seedorf paid a visit to United's Carrington training complex to interview Mainoo for Amazon Prime Video Sport and addressed the fact that Mainoo is often referred to by fans as the "Stockport Seedorf."

"People compare us sometimes, maybe too much. I didn't like to be compared when I was young. I think everybody's unique. I think you're a unique player," the Dutchman told Mainoo.

"I think you have a similar mindset as I had at a young age. The way you read the match and the way you are calm, which is a great attribute to have because when pressure comes for the team, they can rely on you."

Seedorf and Mainoo discussed Champions League matches and the special feeling that the tournament has. Seedorf remains the only player to ever win Europe's biggest club competition with three different clubs.

"It feels like it's so long ago. Well, I know it's only a few years, but it feels like so long ago just because it feels like a lot has happened. A lot of matches and a lot has happened," Mainoo said when asked about his Champions League debut in 2023.

"To be where we are now, you know, obviously we could be doing better in the league, which we will, we will get better. But to be qualified for Champions League and hearing that music and walking out at Old Trafford, you know, is special.

"My first season was my first glimpse of Champions League football and I was young, 18, and I'd come on against Bayern Munich and Galatasaray and I came in the late stages and we were out, so I was like, "Oh, I need to feel that again," you know?

"I need to be under those lights again and to be back there. So it's amazing."

Seedorf spoke about winning the Champions League with his idol Frank Rijkaard and being driven when he was a young player to win as many Champions League titles as Rijkaard did.

He asked Mainoo what his drive is at United and the midfielder said he wants to bring the glory days back to Old Trafford.

"Obviously with a boss like Michael Carrick, who's won here, and he knows about the golden times with Man United, I want to bring that back, you know?" Mainoo told Seedorf.

"I want to feel that. Everyone talks about Manchester United in the past, you know, and I want to bring that to now, and I want to win. I want to win a lot here, you know? That's my dream, for this club to be at the top again."

In response, Seedorf said: "It's beautiful that you talk about your coach.

- Man United could never contend for the Premier League title -- but they aren't so bad either

- Carrick backs Man United for UCL rebound amid challenging spell

- Premier League overreactions: Takeaways from first games post-international break

"Michael has been a great professional, a great player. He will be a great manager as well. He's done good things I've seen from the outside. He brought you back in the pitch -- very smart.

"Having a connection with a coach in a certain part of your career, somebody that believes in you, is so important. I was blessed, I have to say. At a young age as well, I had a lot of coaches believing in me."

United face Atlético Madrid at the Metropolitano Stadium in the Champions League on Tuesday. They will be hoping to get a result and forget their disappointing draw against 10-man Tottenham last time out in the Premier League.

stories.headline: Which NBA deals will get done? Bobby Marks' biggest extension decisions to watch
stories.summary: With Monday's extension deadline looming, Bobby Marks breaks down the biggest decisions around the league.
stories.body:
The NBA season starts in one week, but that isn't the only thing on the minds of league executives. The deadline for rookie extensions is Monday, a day before the 2026-27 regular season tips off.

Since the start of the offseason, five players -- Victor Wembanyama, Amen and Ausar Thompson, Keyonte George and Brandin Podziemski -- have signed rookie extensions. That's currently far below the average of 11 rookie extensions signed per year since 2023, but expect that number to rise in the coming days. Of the 34 players to land rookie extensions in the past three seasons, 17 signed on deadline day.

What deals will the next week bring? We broke down what to expect for six of the 16 eligible players.

Rookie extension decisions aren't the only things we're watching. Oct. 19 is also the deadline to extend veterans with two years remaining on their contract -- not including an option year -- and the deadline to reduce rosters to 15 players on standard contracts.

Let's examine the league's most important extension decisions and what Monday's deadline could bring for teams around the league.

Jump to a section:

Six big rookie extension decisions

KAT, Giannis among vets to watch

Moves coming for Lakers, Knicks?

Rookie extension candidates to watch

Brandon Miller, Charlotte Hornets
Why an extension could get done: Following offseason trades of LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges, the Hornets view Miller and Kon Knueppel as the franchise's new foundation. An injury-plagued sophomore 2024-25 season limited Miller to 27 games, but he rebounded last season to post career highs in 3-pointers made, 3-point percentage and free throw attempts and averaged more than 20 points per game for the second straight season.

Why it might not: Miller views Amen Thompson's five-year, $208 million extension with Houston as a comparable salary. The main difference: Thompson played at least 60 games in each of his first three seasons and was selected for the All-Defensive First Team in 2025.

What I would offer: Five years, $175 million. The contract can either start at $30.2 million and increase each year, ending at $39.8 million, or start high and decline each season. (Coby White's latest contract with the Hornets declines in Years 2 and 3.) With no player earning more than $25 million in 2027-28, Charlotte has the flexibility to increase Miller's offer. Not including new contracts for Miller and center Moussa Diabate, who is eligible for an extension in February, Charlotte projects to be $80 million under the luxury tax next season.

Dereck Lively II, Dallas Mavericks

Why an extension could get done: The Mavericks would need to bypass injury concerns and look at his impact when healthy. Despite playing only 36 games in 2024-25, Lively ranked 17th out of 138 players in offensive rebounding percentage and fourth in defensive rebounding percentage. During that season, Lively held opponents to 56.3% of shooting at the rim, ranking 20th out of 165 players. In 21 postseason games as a rookie, Lively averaged 7.4 rebounds in 22 minutes per game.

Why it might not: What else? Injuries and durability. Lively has played a total of 98 games in his first three seasons, including 55 his rookie year, and missed all but seven games last season. He had right foot surgery in July 2025 before another surgery on the same foot four months later. Lively continues to ramp up his recovery but was not cleared to play 5-on-5 during training camp.

What I would offer: Three years, $35 million. The first-year, $10.8 million salary is comparable to the one-year qualifying offer Lively is eligible for next summer if an extension is not reached. The second year is guaranteed, but the third is contingent on Lively playing at least 41 games in the first or second season of the contract.

Jaime Jaquez Jr., Milwaukee Bucks

Why an extension could get done: If we are evaluating Jaquez off last season with Miami, then discussions for a new contract are warranted. With the Heat, Jaquez became one of four players to average at least 15 points, five rebounds and four assists off the bench since the 1982-83 season. The forward shot a career-high 50.7% last season and saw his assists nearly double from 2.5 to 4.7. Considering Kyle Kuzma is on an expiring contract and Nate Ament is in his rookie season, having Jaquez under contract should be a priority.

Why it might not: Other than failing to reach a compromise, Milwaukee could pause extension talks to evaluate how Jaquez fits in with new Bucks coach Taylor Jenkins.

What I would offer: Four years, $78.8 million. Comparable to Jaquez's free agent hold, the contract starts at $17.8 million and ends with a player option.

Cason Wallace, Oklahoma City Thunder
Why an extension could get done: If there ever was an indication, it was the trade sending Lu Dort to Atlanta.

"I would just say Cason is someone we think very highly of and has done a great job for us," Thunder general manager Sam Presti said before training camp. "I think the greatest sign of respect we could have shown Cason is moving Lu [Dort] in that trade. We potentially could have looked at a series of other options, but it's a bit of a gesture to him to say, 'We think you can have a great role on this team. We believe in you as a player.'"

Named All-Defense for the first time in his career, Wallace led all players in steals last season. He finished seventh in Defensive Player of the Year voting and was one of five guards (Dyson Daniels, Derrick White, Andrew Nembhard, Amen Thompson) over the past two seasons to win Defensive Player of the Month.

Why it might not: Second apron concerns. With Year 1 of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's supermax extension beginning, Oklahoma City is $1.9 million over the second apron. A contract for Wallace starting at $25 million not only puts the Thunder deeper into the apron but will cost them an additional $150 million in luxury taxes. As this past offseason proved with the trades of Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe, Oklahoma City is not afraid to make difficult choices to keep its core intact.

What I would offer: Five years, $145 million. The contract starts at $25 million and increases to $33 million in the final year. You can make a case that Wallace should get more in guaranteed money than Keyonte George and Ausar Thompson, but Oklahoma City is in a different bracket financially than Utah and Detroit.

Anthony Black, Orlando Magic
Why an extension could get done: Past precedent. The Magic have been aggressive in signing former draft picks to rookie extensions. In the past three offseasons, Orlando has extended Cole Anthony, Jalen Suggs, Franz Wagner and Paolo Banchero. If not for injuring his back in early March, Black would have been a candidate for 2026 Most Improved Player; his scoring increased from 9.4 to 15.3 points per game and he shot a career-high 44.7% from the field. Defensively, Black had 25 games with multiple steals.

Why it might not: Finances. A new contract would likely put Orlando over the luxury tax for consecutive seasons and over the first apron. The Magic are a projected $20 million under the tax threshold. Next season and in 2028-29, they will have four players (Wagner, Banchero, Desmond Bane, Jalen Suggs) earning more than $26 million. Considering Orlando has failed to advance past the first round with this roster, is it prudent to pay a significant penalty once again?

What I would offer: There are two ways to look at Black's next contract: the deal Orlando should offer because of its financial constraints, and what Black deserves. If the goal is to remain below the luxury tax, the starting salary cannot exceed $13 million -- below the $16 million non-tax midlevel exception for next season. There is also the question of whether Orlando views him as a starter or a sixth man. The starting backcourt of Suggs and Bane is under contract through at least the 2028-29 season.

Scoot Henderson, Portland Trail Blazers
Why an extension could get done: The Trail Blazers view Henderson's production in the first round of the playoffs as a reason to lock up the former No. 3 pick to a long-term contract. In the first three games against the Spurs, Henderson scored 70 points. Over the past 30 seasons, only Brandon Roy (82 points in 2009) and Damian Lillard (79 points in 2014) scored more through their first three playoﬀ games as a Blazer.

Why it might not: Other than a small sample in the playoffs, what has Henderson done in his first three seasons to show he is worthy of a lucrative contract? Henderson's career field goal percentage (40.4%) is the second worst of any player in the past three seasons. And on defense, Henderson allowed 51.4% shooting from the field as the closest defender last season. Also, how does Henderson fit with new coach Micah Nori and a crowded backcourt of Lillard, Jrue Holiday and Ja Morant?

What I would offer: Three years, $51.8 million. The first-year salary of $16 million is comparable to the non-tax midlevel exception.

Other players eligible for rookie extensions: Noah Clowney (Brooklyn), Julian Strawther (Denver), Marcus Sasser (Dallas), Ben Sheppard (Indiana), Jarace Walker (Indiana), Gradey Dick (LA Clippers), Taylor Hendricks (Memphis), Kris Murray (Memphis), Brice Sensabaugh (Utah), Bilal Coulibaly (Washington)

Veteran extension candidates

Recent extensions for Kawhi Leonard and Stephen Curry have continued the trend of stars choosing guaranteed money over hitting free agency. Since the offseason started in July, 11 potential free agents extended their contracts, including Leonard, Curry and Donovan Mitchell.

There are two sets of deadlines for players who are extension-eligible. For players with two years or more remaining on their contract, such as the Celtics' Payton Pritchard, Monday is the deadline to extend. Players with one year remaining on their contract have until June 30 to extend.

If a player has two years left on his contract but with an option in the last season, however, he is also eligible to extend up to June 30. This group includes Nikola Jokic, Karl-Anthony Towns, Giannis Antetokounmpo and Anthony Davis. For each of the four players to extend after Oct. 19, the player option must be eliminated and replaced with the first year of the extension.

Here are where things stand ahead of that Oct. 19 deadline:

Nikola Jokic, Denver Nuggets
For the second consecutive offseason, Jokic will not sign an extension in Denver. The lack of long-term security has nothing to do with his unhappiness in Denver, but rather his ability to maximize finances next offseason. By waiting until the 2027 offseason, Jokic is eligible to sign a five-year, $359.5 million contract as a free agent. That contract would be the largest in NBA history and see his career on-court earnings reach $724 million.

Karl-Anthony Towns, New York Knicks

Towns has repeatedly said the goal is to get a new contract done with New York.

"Simply put, I want to do something that can keep the team together and work with the Knicks and also values me," Towns said on Oct. 5. The Knicks are thinking differently, stating they will not negotiate any extensions until later in the season.

Since the NBA Finals concluded in mid-June, Towns has been eligible to sign up to a four-year, $276 million extension. Talks have reached an impasse, per Towns, however. "None of those things have come close to happening," he said.

The holdup on why New York is not writing a blank check comes down to second apron concerns over the foreseeable future. With Towns' $61 million player option in 2027-28, New York is likely to exceed the second apron. They are currently $9 million below the threshold and have five open roster spots. The purse strings get even tighter in the summer of 2028.

Not including new contracts for Towns and Josh Hart and a significant raise for Jalen Brunson (his salary will likely increase from $43.3 to $64.7 million), New York will project to be $104 million below the second apron.

For example, if New York signed Towns to a four-year, $227 million extension ($53 million, $57.4 million, $61.5 million and $65.7 million), extended Hart starting at $20 million and signed Brunson to a max contract, it guarantees New York as a second apron team for the 2028-29 season. Knicks owner James Dolan said after the Finals that New York will not exceed the second apron.

Giannis Antetokounmpo, Miami Heat
Antetokounmpo has been extension-eligible since Oct. 1 but at considerably less money because he was traded on July 6. The extension would be either three years, $194 million or two years, $135.1 million. But waiting until Jan. 6 (six months after the trade) would make Antetokounmpo eligible to sign a four-year, $276 million extension. The $62.8 million player option would be replaced with Year 1 of the extension.

One scenario not to be overlooked: Antetokounmpo mirroring Jokic and re-signing with Miami as a free agent in the 2027 offseason. By not extending in January, Antetokounmpo would then become eligible for a five-year, $357 million contract. His potential $754 million in career on court earnings would be the most in NBA history.

Anthony Davis, Washington Wizards

Do not expect a Davis extension in the near future.

"[I'll decide] when the season is over," Davis said on media day. "We're going to go through the season and try to do what I do at a high level. ... And then when it's over, sit down and have those conversations again with the front office."

Davis became eligible to sign an extension in early August for up to four years and $275 million. He holds a player option for $62 million next season, the final year of a three-year, $175 million deal he signed with the Lakers. The first year of an extension would replace that player option. Davis, 33, did not play with Washington after he was acquired at last season's trade deadline, and he has failed to reach 60 games in five of the past six seasons.

Jaden McDaniels, Minnesota Timberwolves

McDaniels is eligible to extend for two years and $87 million. (Because he has three years remaining on his current contract, the first year of the extension would not start until 2029-30.) Last season, McDaniels increased his scoring from 14.8 points per game in the regular season to 16.5 in the playoffs and scored a season-high 32 points in the Game 6 clincher against Denver. In that series, McDaniels also held All-Star Jamal Murray to 32% shooting as the closest defender.

Payton Pritchard, Boston Celtics

Pritchard has two years remaining on his contract and through Monday can tack on three additional seasons and $67 million. The first year of an extension would make him the third-highest-paid Celtic in 2028-29. In 79 games last season (50 starts), Pritchard averaged 17.0 points and 5.2 assists per game. His current $7.8 million salary remains one of the best bargains in the NBA.

More players to watch

Oct. 19 deadline: Onyeka Okongwu (Atlanta), Terance Mann (Brooklyn), Royce O'Neale (Charlotte), Nicolas Claxton (Chicago), Moses Moody (Golden State), Pascal Siakam (Indiana), Obi Toppin (Indiana), Andrew Nembhard (Indiana), Tyrese Haliburton (Indiana), Ivica Zubac (Indiana), Darius Garland (LA Clippers), Anthony Edwards (Minnesota), LaMelo Ball (Minnesota), Jaden McDaniels (Minnesota), Karlo Matkovic (New Orleans), Zion Williamson (New Orleans), Desmond Bane (Orlando), Jaylen Brown (Philadelphia), Deni Avdija (Portland), Ja Morant (Portland), Domantas Sabonis (Sacramento), Devin Vassell (San Antonio).

June 30 deadline: Lu Dort (Atlanta), Mouhamed Gueye (Atlanta), Paul George (Boston), Michael Porter Jr. (Brooklyn), Grant Williams (Charlotte), Leonard Miller (Chicago), Jalen Smith (Chicago), Isaac Okoro (Chicago), Buddy Hield (Chicago), Craig Porter Jr. (Cleveland), Max Christie (Dallas), Caleb Martin (Dallas), Cameron Johnson (Denver), Zeke Nnaji (Denver), Johnny Furphy (Indiana), Jay Huff (Indiana), Kris Dunn (LA Clippers), Derrick Jones Jr. (LA Clippers), Cam Christie (LA Clippers), Max Strus (LA Clippers), Jarred Vanderbilt (LA Lakers), Bronny James (LA Lakers), Jaden Hardy (LA Lakers), Isaiah Stewart (Memphis), Jaylen Wells (Memphis), Scotty Pippen Jr. (Memphis), Jerami Grant (Memphis), Giannis Antetokounmpo (Miami), Kyle Kuzma (Milwaukee), Tyler Herro (Milwaukee), Donte DiVincenzo (Minnesota), Rudy Gobert (Minnesota), Jordan Poole (New Orleans), Dejounte Murray (New Orleans), Josh Hart (New York), Tyler Kolek (New York), Miles McBride (New York), Goga Bitadze (Orlando), Adem Bona (Philadelphia), Jalen Green (Phoenix), Oso Ighodaro (Phoenix), Miles Bridges (Phoenix), Vit Krejci (Portland), Zach LaVine (Sacramento), De'Andre Hunter (Sacramento), Malik Monk (Sacramento), Keldon Johnson (San Antonio), Kyle Filopowski (Utah), Svi Mykhailiuk (Utah).

Key roster decisions around the league

Nearly 80 players will hit waivers Saturday night in anticipation of Monday's deadline to cut rosters to 15 players. Teams will incur a per-day cap hit if a player signed to a non-guaranteed contract is not waived by 5 p.m. ET on Saturday. For example, the Knicks would be charged $17,622 per day against the cap if James Wiseman is not waived by Saturday. New York is currently over the luxury tax and first apron. The full salary counts against the apron.

Here are three more teams to watch as the Monday roster deadline approaches:

Los Angeles Lakers
Is there a trade on the horizon to consolidate the Lakers' roster? With 16 players currently on guaranteed contracts, Los Angeles will need to open up a roster spot either in a trade or by releasing a player.

"Behind that evaluation of who's emerging in camp, there's also consolidation trades that could still be looked at -- trading two guys out, bringing one in," Lakers president of basketball operations Rob Pelinka said last month. "There's a number of ways that could be addressed."

Memphis Grizzlies
The Grizzlies have already made two roster decisions by waiving veteran D'Angelo Russell and former first-round pick Jordan Hawkins.

Memphis has 16 guaranteed contracts but needs to release two players because the $2.3 million salary of Jaylen Wells is set to become guaranteed on Oct. 19. Possible candidates include Kris Murray and Micah Peavy.

New York Knicks

New York loaded up on depth this summer by signing veterans Bruce Brown, Ochai Agbaji, Drew Eubanks, James Wiseman and Tony Bradley. But due to a self-imposed second apron hard cap, the Knicks are likely to keep just one of the five players despite having two open roster spots. They are currently $3.2 million below the second apron. Other options: Keep two players and then cut one during the season, or make a minor trade to clear out salary.

Other decisions to watch

The Hornets made a series of transactions in the offseason, trading Dorian Finney-Smith, Buddy Hield and waiving Ryan Nembhard. They have 16 players on standard contracts, including the non-guaranteed contract of veteran Pat Connaughton.
With Moussa Cisse's contract becoming guaranteed on Oct. 1, Dallas has 15 players on guaranteed deals. The Mavericks signed center Dwight Powell before training camp and need to waive the veteran or make another move to get their roster to 15 players.
The Warriors have a decision with their final two roster spots. They are hard-capped at the second apron and allowed to keep only three of these four players: Brandon Williams, Dalen Terry, Georges Niang and Charles Bassey. Terry, whose contract is not guaranteed, had a team-high 23 points in a preseason loss to the Trail Blazers on Oct. 7. Bassey ($1.4 million) and Niang's ($1.8 million) salaries are partially guaranteed, while Williams' salary increases from no protection to $1.4 million if he is not waived on the first day of the regular season.
The Clippers and Cam Christie agreed to move back his guaranteed date twice during the offseason. Now with a Thursday deadline looming, LA can guarantee the former second-round pick and waive a player on a guaranteed deal -- newly acquired Gradey Dick, for example -- or cut bait with Christie.
The four-for-one trade that sent Antetokounmpo to Miami has Milwaukee with 16 guaranteed contracts. Pete Nance's deal becomes guaranteed if he is not waived by Monday.

stories.headline: Brendan Allen submits his case for moving up in MMA divisional rankings
stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
Brendan Allen fought a back-and-forth battle with Christian Leroy Duncan in Saturday's UFC Fight Night main event. Going into the fifth round of the meeting of top-10 middleweights, Allen was narrowly ahead on all three scorecards. Of course, he did not know what the judges were thinking.

So Allen took it out of the judges' hands in Round 5, getting Duncan to the ground and efficiently finishing the gritty fight with a rear-naked choke.

With his fourth straight victory, Allen moves up one spot to No. 5 in the ESPN divisional rankings, continuing his recent climb in the middleweight top 10.

That's the only rankings change this week. Duncan remains No. 10 at 185 pounds, and sixth-ranked strawweight Loopy Godínez, who beat unranked Ketlen Souza by decision on Saturday's undercard, also retains her spot.

stories.headline: Christian Horner: Mercedes' Toto Wolff has it 'easy' at the moment
stories.summary: Former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner has suggested that Mercedes boss Toto Wolff has "got it quite easy" at the moment.
stories.body:
Former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner has suggested that Mercedes boss Toto Wolff has "got it quite easy" at the moment.

Horner, 52, officially left Red Bull Racing in September last year having been relieved of "operational duties" following last July's British Grand Prix. It ended a 20-year career with the team, where he won eight drivers' and six constructors' titles.

The past decade saw Horner spar with Wolff as Red Bull and Mercedes did battle.

This season, Horner's old team are currently fourth in the constructors' standings with 11 podiums and two wins, both claimed by Max Verstappen during this month's races in Bahrain and Singapore.

Mercedes top the constructors' leaderboard, while Kimi Antonelli is first in the drivers' standings having won eight races so far.

A potential return to F1 for Horner remains a hot topic and in an interview earlier this year, Wolff suggested Horner had "broken a lot of glass."

In an interview with the Guardian, Horner said: "He [Wolff] also said this [Red Bull] engine was going to be completely s--t and a disaster.

"Toto's got it quite easy at the moment. Zak Brown [head of McLaren] is compromised because he's using Toto's engine so he can't ruffle feathers.

"All sport needs rivalry, whether it's [Alex] Ferguson and [Arsene] Wenger, [Jose] Mourinho and (Pep) Guardiola. It percolates and polarises. I used that to galvanise good people to take on Mercedes."

- Formula 1 to return to Africa in 'early 2030s' as Rwanda race confirmed

- 'Chucky' Verstappen is back. Luckily for Antonelli and Mercedes, it's too late

- Toto Wolff finds quirky solution to Kimi Antonelli track limits 'stress'

Horner also revealed in the interview that he has suffered from panic attacks and has worked to recognise the symptoms.

"I didn't know what it was. You suddenly feel dizzy and conscious of your breathing and you think there's something strange going on. I put it down to having had too much coffee on an oppressive, muggy, thundery day," he said.

"Then it happened again. I got checked out and there was nothing physically the matter. They said: 'We think you have anxiety. Your breathing's very shallow.' It was my body telling me you're pushing pretty hard here. I'm able to recognise the symptoms now and let it go, and breathe."

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little earlier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Tuesday, Oct. 13
Blues land gun Giant

Lachie Whitfield's move to Carlton is official, with the 32-year-old joining the Blues on a three-year deal. Whitfield has played 278 games, and joins Toby Greene, Jesse Hogan, and Jake Stringer in departing the Giants.

Carlton receive picks 31 and 50 along with the veteran, with pick 25, pick 26, and a 2028 third-round pick going back the other way.

Former top-five pick on the move

Zane Duursma has got his wish, joining Melbourne along with pick 52. The Roos get pick 33 and 49 in return.

Blues ruck crosses to Collingwood

Flynn Riley has been traded to the Magpies after joining Carlton in the mid-season draft this year, making his AFL debut in Round 18.

A 2028 third-round pick goes the Blues' way.

Swans trade star defender to North Melbourne

The biggest name left on the AFL trade board has tumbled, with Sydney agreeing to move Nick Blakey to North Melbourne.

The Swans offloaded Blakey, draft pick No.52 and their 2028 second-round selection in exchange for a glut of picks.

The Kangaroos traded picks No.6 and No.47, a 2027 second-round pick, a 2028 first-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick to get the deal done.

Monday Oct. 12
Suns land Schubert, Butler from Hawks

The Suns have landed their offseason trade target in Aidan Schubert from Hawthorn, in a package also involving Sam Butler and some picks going both ways.

Gold Coast gained Schubert, Butler, Hawthorn's 2028 first-round pick, and Hawthorn's 2027 third-round pick, in exchange for Gold Coast's 2028 first-rounder, and second rounders in both 2027 and 2028.

Friday, Oct. 9
Butters is a Bulldog

Zak Butters is officially a Western Bulldog. Port Adelaide will not match the offer and accept pick No. 5 as compensation, having also earlier secured picks 6, 10, and two future-firsts in the five-club mega trade. The star free agent and three-time All-Australian, who played 156 games and kicked 73 goals for the Power after being drafted in 2019, has signed a nine-year deal with his boyhood club

Hawks land spearhead King

After securing Zach Merrett earlier this week, Hawthorn have officially welcomed Ben King today after gold Coast elected not to match the offer for the restricted free agent. the Suns will receive a first round pick as compensation, which currently stands at pick No. 7.

Mega trade approved

The league approved a mega trade involving Port Adelaide, the Bulldogs, Melbourne, Hawthorn and Carlton, two players and scores of picks.

Under the five-team deal, the Bulldogs gave up picks No. 12 and No. 31 and a 2028 first-rounder to bring in Hawthorn's Finn Maginness, Carlton's Hudson O'Keeffe and later picks in this year's draft and future years.

Port parted with picks No. 4, 46 and 81 and six second-round or worse future selections to get back picks No. 6 and No. 10, Melbourne's 2027 first-rounder and the Dogs' 2028 first-rounder.

The Demons surrendered picks No.6, 10 and 87 and their 2027 first-rounder -- as well as two late future picks -- for picks No. 4, 12, 31 and 46.

Hawthorn (2027 third-rounder) and Carlton (2028 fourth-rounder) received late future picks for Maginness and O'Keeffe.

-- AAP

Flag Lion gets his wish

Brisbane has traded second-year Lion and 2025 premiership player Sam Marshall and pick No. 39 to St Kilda for a 2027 first-rounder.

Thursday, Oct. 8
Marshall lands at the Cats

St Kilda have pulled the trigger on a deal to send contracted ruckman Rowan Marshall to Geelong, as the Cats and other rival clubs circle Sydney star Nick Blakey.

Geelong traded pick No.14 in this year's draft for the disenchanted 30-year-old and a third-round selection in 2028 on Thursday afternoon.

New Zealand-born Marshall had requested a move to the Cats for a second straight year after St Kilda recruited Tom De Koning to become their first-choice ruckman.

-- AAP

Wednesday, Oct. 7
Dons defender gets traded to the Cats

After being denied a trade last year, Jordan Ridley got his wish for a fresh start after Essendon and Geelong agreed to a deal on Wednesday.

Geelong gave up utility Jack Bowes, a 2027 first-round pick and 2028 second-round pick to get the 27-year-old Ridley through the door.

Pick No. 60 and a 2028 fourth-round selection will come back to the Cats from the Bombers.

--AAP

Tuesday, Oct. 6
O'Driscoll makes the move over east

Fremantle have traded 24-year-old Nathan O'Driscoll to Richmond in exchange for pick 61 in this year's draft.

The winger played 17 games for the Dockers this season but wasn't selected for the Grand Final.

Monday, Oct. 5
TRADE PERIOD OPENS
Merrett finally becomes a Hawk

After attempting to join Hawthorn last year, Zach Merrett has finally been traded from Essendon to the Hawks.

Hawthorn have sent picks 15, 25 and a 2028 second-round pick in exchange for the 31-year-old.

Merrett leaves the Bombers a week after winning a record-equaling seventh Crichton Medal, three All-Australian blazers, and 274 games.

Pendlebury becomes a Sun

AFL games record holder Scott Pendlebury is officially a Sun after Gold Coast and Collingwood agreed on a trade for the 38-year-old veteran.

Pendlebury, a two-time premiership player, heads to the Suns in exchange for pick No. 65 in this year's draft.

"It's an exciting group here at the SUNS and the opportunity to bring a few different ideas and also learn from a great group of coaches and players is one I'm really looking forward to," Pendlebury told the Suns.

"This side is one I've watched from afar and really admired. I've got a bit of knowledge about the industry so I'm here to play my role and help this squad continue to develop."

Jesse Hogan traded from GWS to Collingwood

Out-of-favour Giants forward Jesse Hogan has made the switch to Collingwood in exchange for pick 75.

The 31-year-old won the Coleman Medal in 2024 but has been unable to recapture his best form at the Giants in the two years since.

Magpies list boss Justin Leppitsch said Hogan would be a valuable addition.

"On behalf of everyone at Collingwood, I'd like to warmly welcome Jesse to Collingwood. Jesse has established himself as one of the competition's premier key forwards and we're excited to see him bring his experience and talent to our club," he said.

"His aerial presence inside forward-50 and his consistency as a goal-kicker make him a genuine threat.

"Like Lachie (Neale), Jesse has a passion to teach the next generation and will make a great addition to our club."

Saturday, Oct. 3
Bulldogs seal free-agency signing of key defender

The Western Bulldogs have finally snagged the key defender they need, securing Adelaide backman Jordon Butts as an unrestricted free agent.

The Bulldogs are set for a bumper AFL trade period headlined by working through a deal for Port Adelaide superstar Zak Butters, ahead of a 2027 season where the club will have high expectations.

But after seeing off Carlton's advances to keep hold of defender Buku Khamis, the Bulldogs have filled a major area of need by adding 26-year-old Butts.

Adelaide will receive a second-round compensation selection, currently pick No.33, in this year's draft.

-- AAP

Friday, Oct. 2
FREE AGENCY OPEN
Three-peat Lion locks in Magpies move

Lachie Neale has sealed his high-profile switch to Collingwood, with Brisbane teasing the dual Brownlow medallist on his way out the door.

The AFL approved Neale signing a three-year deal with the Magpies on Friday afternoon, closing out the first day of free agency.

The 33-year-old ball-winner leaves as an unrestricted free agent after the Lions clinched a third straight flag with their stunning seven-point grand final victory over Fremantle.

-- AAP

Greene on his way to the Cats

Toby Greene will join Geelong as an unrestricted free agent on a three-year deal, re-partnering with former Giants teammate Jeremey Cameron.

The paperwork was lodged to the AFL on Friday morning.

The Giants receive band three compensation for Greene, which is currently pick No. 26 in the upcoming draft.

Greene departs the Giants with his name etched in the club's record books, sitting first in games played for the club with a tally of 282 games, as well as leading the club's all-time goalkicking tally with 450 majors.

Briggs now a Tiger

Richmond has landed GWS ruck Kieren Briggs as an unrestricted free agent.

Briggs' move to the Tigers was confirmed just hours after the free agency window opened on Friday.

Briggs played 88 games for GWS after joining the club as the No.34 pick in the 2018 draft.

Amartey officially joins the Blues

Free agency has opened with a bang, with out-of-favour key forward Joel Amartey committing to Carlton.

Details are still to come on the length of contract, and Sydney's compensation.

Hawthorn father-son recommits despite interest

Calsher Dear has made a shock decision to re-sign with the Hawks for two years, despite being out of favour thorughout 2026.

The 20-year-old has kicked 39 goals from 31 games, but found himself behind Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis and Mabior Chol. With Gunston signed on and Suns forward Ben King expected to sign with the Hawks as well, there were questions about whether Dear would get enough opportunity at his childhood club.

Hawks list boss Mark McKenzie said the club was "really pleased" that Dear had recommitted.

"He remains an important part of what we are trying to achieve as a club," he said.

"Following his debut season, Calsher showed us all the special talent that he is, but as a key tall at 21 years of age, we've needed to be patient with his progression.

"Having battled several injuries over his first three seasons in the system, we are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond."

Thursday, Oct. 1
Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.
